intro: This course covered food allergies and intolerances, the 14 named allergens and labelling law, safe support, and recognising and responding to reactions.
points: Anaphylaxis is a medical emergency — if you see it, use a prescribed adrenaline auto-injector per the care plan, call 999 and say you think it is anaphylaxis.
A true food allergy involves the immune system and can be life-threatening, while an intolerance does not — take every allergy extremely seriously.
A mild reaction can turn severe within minutes, so keep watching closely and always stay with the person.
Remember UK law names 14 allergens that must be declared, and Natasha's Law means PPDS foods carry a full ingredients list.
Never guess — if you are not certain a food is safe, say "let me check" and read the label or care plan every time.
Prevent cross-contamination by washing hands, using separate clean utensils and surfaces, and keeping allergen-free meals apart.
